source_summary: As of 2026-07-07, HearthSim deckstrings is an appropriate primary source for exact deckstring decode because the spec and reference implementation losslessly decode hero DBF IDs, card DBF/count pairs, format, and sideboards. HearthstoneJSON `cards.json` is an appropriate primary source for DBF-to-CardID mapping, card text, and broad static mechanics because it publishes unique `id`, `dbfId`, localized `text`, `mechanics`, and hero-card `heroPowerDbfId`, and it includes non-collectible cards. However, a live 2026-07-07 probe of `https://api.hearthstonejson.com/v1/latest/enUS/cards.json` showed `heroPowerDbfId` on 2,988 rows and `questReward` on 9 rows, but `entourage` on 0 rows and `playRequirements` on 0 rows, so HearthstoneJSON alone is not a complete current source for generated-entity closure or Shadowform-style hero-power transform identity.
current_truth: Treat HearthSim/deckstrings as the decode authority and treat HearthstoneJSON `cards.json` as the normalized registry for `dbfId` <-> `CardID`, localized text, card type, and most mechanic tags. Do not treat HearthstoneJSON alone as sufficient for all generated entities or hero-power transform identity. For HSConfig, the lean correct design on 2026-07-07 is: decode deck codes with HearthSim/deckstrings, map DBF IDs to CardIDs with HearthstoneJSON or another full card registry, and add a deterministic supplement layer for generated links and Shadowform-style hero-power replacement when the live JSON payload does not expose a structured link.
repo_alignment: HSConfig already aligns with the safe parts of this conclusion. `README.md` states that `hsconfig prepare` decodes deck codes through HearthSim deckstrings and enriches static card semantics. `src/hsconfig/deckstring_decode.py` already uses `hearthstone.deckstrings.parse_deckstring`, but it resolves DBF IDs through `hearthstone.cardxml.load_dbf()` rather than HearthstoneJSON. `src/hsconfig/hearthstonejson.py` already normalizes HearthstoneJSON fields such as `id`, `dbfId`, `text`, `mechanics`, `referencedTags`, `heroPowerDbfId`, `questReward`, `playRequirements`, and `entourage`. `src/hsconfig/semantic_enrichment.py` also already encodes the key risk: it carries a built-in `Mind Spike` fallback because Shadowform and Darkbishop Benedictus do not arrive as a clean structured hero-power-transform link from the source data alone.
gaps_or_risks: If HSConfig treats HearthstoneJSON as the only source of generated-entity relationships, it will currently miss links that are not exposed through `heroPowerDbfId` or `questReward`; the live 2026-07-07 `cards.json` probe returned zero `entourage` and zero `playRequirements` rows.
HearthSim/deckstrings is not a DBF-to-CardID mapper; it yields DBF-based deck identity, not normalized CardIDs or text. A second registry layer is mandatory after decode.

Shadowform-style hero-power replacement is only textually visible in current HearthstoneJSON rows such as `EX1_625` and `SW_448`; there is no direct structured field on those rows that names `EX1_625t` or `EX1_625t2` as the replacement hero powers.
Generated-entity closure from plain text is unsafe for runtime writes because text describes effects but does not reliably encode the exact emitted CardID, pool, branch, or upgrade target.

HearthstoneJSON documentation still describes fields like `entourage` and `playRequirements`, so HSConfig should explicitly guard against documentation-versus-payload drift instead of assuming every documented field family is populated in the current live feed.
recommended_action: Keep HearthSim/deckstrings for deck decode. Use HearthstoneJSON `cards.json` as the first normalized card registry for `dbfId`/`CardID`, text, type, and mechanics. Preserve the current supplement strategy for hero-power transform and generated-link gaps, but formalize it: add an explicit deterministic linkage layer for required non-deck entities such as transformed hero powers, quest rewards, and generated cards, and fail closed when a required exact CardID cannot be proven from structured source data.
